name: Open multilingual decoder LLMs fine-tuned with LoRA as sequence classifiers (Qwen3 / Qwen3-Reranker, Gemma 3 (and Gemma 4), Llama 3.1/3.2/3.3, Salamandra)
links: Qwen3 tech report arXiv:2505.09388, HF Qwen/Qwen3-{0.6B,1.7B,4B,8B,14B,32B}(-Base), cross-encoder variants Qwen/Qwen3-Reranker-{0.6B,4B,8B}; Gemma 3 tech report arXiv:2503.19786, HF google/gemma-3-{1b,4b,12b,27b}-pt/-it; Llama 3 herd arXiv:2407.21783, HF meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B, Llama-3.2-{1B,3B}, Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct; Salamandra tech report arXiv:2502.08489, HF BSC-LT/salamandra-{2b,7b}(-instruct); label-supervised LoRA classification: LS-LLaMA arXiv:2310.01208; HF blog 'LoRA for sequence classification with RoBERTa, Llama and Mistral' (github.com/huggingface/blog/blob/main/Lora-for-sequence-classification-with-Roberta-Llama-Mistral.md); bidirectional conversion LLM2Vec arXiv:2404.05961; Iberian compact-LLM eval (XNLI eu/es/ca) arXiv:2504.03312; PEFT github.com/huggingface/peft. Newer 2026 open families (Gemma 4, Qwen3.5) exist and should be treated as drop-in candidates [uncertain].
year: Llama 3.1 (Jul 2024), Llama 3.2 (Sep 2024), Llama 3.3 (Dec 2024); Salamandra (Sep 2024, report Feb 2025); Gemma 3 (Mar 2025); Qwen3 (Apr 2025), Qwen3-Reranker (Jun 2025); Gemma 4 (Apr 2026) and Qwen3.5 (Feb-Mar 2026) [uncertain]
license_access: All open-weight. Qwen3 / Qwen3-Reranker: Apache 2.0. Salamandra: Apache 2.0. Gemma 3: Gemma Terms of Use (open weights, use-policy restrictions, gated download). Llama 3.x: Llama 3.1/3.2/3.3 Community License (gated on HF, acceptable-use policy, 700M MAU clause). Gemma 4 reportedly Apache 2.0 [uncertain]. All run locally on the remote GPU box; no API.
track_coverage: Technically all four tracks (T1 EN, T2 ES, T3 EU, T4 mixed) with one multilingual checkpoint. Strongest fit: T1/T2 (all four families are strong in English and Spanish). T3/T4 depend on Basque competence, which varies sharply by family (Salamandra > Gemma 3 >= Qwen3 > Llama 3.x without Basque adaptation; Latxa is the Basque-specialised Llama and is covered as a separate item). A single model trained jointly on T1-T4 rows (all views share pair_id) is the natural setup.
basque_quality: Salamandra: Basque is one of 35 pre-training languages (explicitly Iberian-focused, BSC); on zero-shot XNLI-eu (lm-eval, arXiv:2504.03312 Table 6) Salamandra-7B-it 0.475, Salamandra-7B base 0.456, Salamandra-2B-it 0.430 vs Llama-3.1-8B-it 0.411, Qwen2.5-7B-it 0.400, Gemma-2-9B-it 0.449, Mistral-Small-3-24B 0.455 (same paper, es: Salamandra-7B 0.507, Llama-3.1-8B-it 0.494). Llama 3.x: Basque not among the 8 officially supported languages; Latxa papers show large Basque gains from continued pretraining, implying vanilla Llama is weak in EU. Gemma 3: advertises 140+ languages with a 262k tokenizer; Basque is covered in pretraining but no official EU NLI number [uncertain]. Qwen3: 119 languages/dialects claimed; Basque listed in coverage [uncertain], quality on EU presumed below ES/EN. Important caveat: zero-shot XNLI numbers of 7-9B models are near 0.40-0.48 (3-way, chance 0.33), so they say little about fine-tuned performance; fine-tuned multilingual encoders reach ~81-84% on XNLIeu (XLM-R large, arXiv:2404.06996). Expect LoRA-fine-tuned 7-12B LLMs to be at least competitive with XLM-R-large on EU, but no published EU phrase-level NLI number exists [uncertain].
cross_lingual_robustness: Large multilingual LLMs have shared semantic spaces that usually give small EN->ES gaps (a few points) and larger EN->EU gaps. Because T4 pairs mix languages inside one input (e.g. en-eu), a decoder must align across scripts/lexicons inside the context window; LLMs with strong EU coverage (Salamandra, Gemma 3/4) should degrade less. Expected ordering of difficulty: en-en < es-es ~ en-es < eu-eu ~ en-eu/es-eu. Training on all 12 mixed views plus monolingual views (same source pairs) acts as cross-lingual augmentation and should shrink the gap; pooling predictions across views of the same pair_id at test time removes most residual language variance (see view-aggregation item). Gap estimate for a fine-tuned 8B model: 2-4 F1 points ES vs EN, 5-10 points EU vs EN [uncertain].
architecture: Decoder-only causal transformers (Qwen3: GQA, RoPE, QK-norm, dense and MoE variants; Gemma 3: interleaved local/global attention 5:1, 128k context; Llama 3.x: GQA, 128k vocab; Salamandra: Llama-style dense decoder trained from scratch, 256k vocab). For classification: *ForSequenceClassification head = linear layer on the hidden state of the last non-pad token, trained with cross-entropy on 4 labels; LoRA (r=8-64, alpha=2r) on all attention and MLP projections, head trained fully (modules_to_save=['score']). Input template e.g. 'Phrase A: {text1}\nPhrase B: {text2}\nRelation of A to B:' so the last token attends to both phrases. Key design issue for DiCo: causal attention makes the representation order-asymmetric (text1 tokens never see text2), the reversal-curse setting the pilot highlights; mitigations: (1) always run both orders and use joint pair decoding; (2) remove the causal mask during fine-tuning (LS-unLLaMA / LLM2Vec style bidirectional attention); (3) antisymmetric head built from h(a,b) and h(b,a). Alternative: Qwen3-Reranker is already a pairwise cross-encoder (yes/no logit), a good initialization for a relatedness gate.
params: Qwen3: 0.6B, 1.7B, 4B, 8B, 14B, 32B dense; 30B-A3B and 235B-A22B MoE. Qwen3-Reranker: 0.6B/4B/8B. Gemma 3: 1B, 4B, 12B, 27B. Llama 3.1: 8B/70B/405B; 3.2: 1B/3B; 3.3: 70B. Salamandra: 2B, 7B (and 40B / ALIA-40b). LoRA adds ~0.1-1% trainable params (e.g. ~20-80M for an 8B model at r=16-64).
compute: Inputs are tiny (phrases average ~6 words per pair; ~30-60 tokens with template), so memory is dominated by weights. bf16 LoRA: 1-4B fits easily in 24 GB; 7-9B (Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, Salamandra-7B) needs ~17-20 GB weights, fits 24 GB with gradient checkpointing and batch 16-32, comfortable on 40-48 GB; 12-14B needs 40-48 GB (or QLoRA in 24 GB); 27-32B needs 80 GB for bf16 LoRA or ~20-24 GB with 4-bit QLoRA; 70B requires QLoRA on 48-80 GB. Time: T1-T3 train sets are 3,042 rows; T4 18,252 rows; one epoch of an 8B model on all ~27k rows at seq len 64 takes ~5-15 min on a single A100/H100 [uncertain]; 5-fold x 3 seeds x 3 epochs for 8B is a few GPU-hours. Flash-attention / SDPA and packing are optional given short inputs.
sample_efficiency: Only ~1,282 reversible source pairs (+478 NEGATIVE_OTHER singletons) per monolingual track (~1.8k source items), multiplied by 2 orders x 15 language views. LLM LoRA classifiers are generally more sample-efficient than encoders of similar quality because of stronger priors (LS-LLaMA beats RoBERTa-large on small classification sets), but they are known to have high seed variance and to overfit after 2-3 epochs on few-thousand-example sets; the pilot already reports strong hyperparameter sensitivity even for small models. Mitigations: low LR (1e-4 to 2e-4 for LoRA, 1e-5 for head warmup), 2-3 epochs, grouped CV by pair_id (views of the same pair must never straddle folds), ensembling 3-5 seeds/folds, and an intermediate NLI stage (MNLI/XNLI/XNLIeu, 3-way) before DiCo fine-tuning. Expect seed std of 1-3 F1 points at 8B [uncertain].
reported_results: No DiCo-NLI or PhrasIS result exists for these families. Related evidence: (1) LS-LLaMA (Llama-2-7B + LoRA, label-supervised) outperforms BERT-large/RoBERTa-large on several text-classification benchmarks and LLMs 10x larger used via prompting (arXiv:2310.01208). (2) LoRA-fine-tuned 7-8B decoders typically reach ~90-92% MNLI-m, on par with or slightly above DeBERTa-v3-large (~91.8) [uncertain]. (3) Zero-shot XNLI (lm-eval, arXiv:2504.03312): eu Salamandra-7B-it 0.475, Llama-3.1-8B-it 0.411, Gemma-2-9B-it 0.449, Qwen2.5-7B-it 0.400; es Salamandra-7B 0.507, Llama-3.1-8B-it 0.494 - i.e. prompting small open LLMs is not competitive; fine-tuning is required. (4) XNLIeu with fine-tuned XLM-R-large: 83.8 translate-train, 81.1 zero-shot transfer (arXiv:2404.06996); Latxa prompting 50.9 - reference points for what fine-tuned LLMs must beat on EU. (5) Pilot LREC 2026: small decoder-only models (OPT/Pythia/GPT-2, 117-410M) were the weakest family (best Positives-A F1 0.62 GPT-2 M; unseen SoftCoh 0.65 OPT-125M; unseen HardCoh 0.58), but these are not modern multilingual LLMs and were fine-tuned fully, not with LoRA at 7B+ scale.
pilot_dico_results: Not evaluated in the LREC 2026 pilot (Apaolaza Larraya et al., 'Assessing Logical Coherence of LLMs via Fine-Grained NLI'). The pilot only covered small decoder-only models (OPT 125M/350M, Pythia 160M/410M, GPT-2 S/M) on English PhrasIS: Positives-A weighted F1 0.52-0.62, unseen SoftCoh Positives-A 0.47-0.65, unseen HardCoh Positives-A 0.38-0.58, versus DeBERTa-v3-base 0.75/0.84/0.79. The pilot explicitly states that large proprietary models were not evaluated and attributes decoder weakness to lack of bidirectional context; whether 7B+ multilingual LLMs close this gap is an open question this item would test.
consistency_guarantee: none (plain LoRA classifier). Becomes inference-time if combined with joint pair decoding, soft if trained with reversal-consistency loss, architectural only with an antisymmetric head over h(a,b)/h(b,a).
negative_other_handling: Treated as a 4th class by the classification head; the model can and will emit NEGATIVE_OTHER on gold-reversible pairs, which zeroes SoftCons and HardCons for that pair (the official scorer only counts a pair as soft-consistent when the first prediction is one of EQ/FE/BE). Class balance: NEG is ~16% of rows. Recommended: keep the 4-way head but decide NEG with a tuned threshold or a separate relatedness gate (Qwen3-Reranker-style yes/no is a natural fit), and apply the pair-level NEG gate in joint decoding.
metric_tradeoff: Expected to raise Weighted F1 over DeBERTa-style encoders on T2/T3/T4 (stronger multilingual knowledge, world knowledge for cases like 'German shepherd' -> 'black dog' errors cited in the pilot), possibly neutral on T1. Raw SoftCons likely lower than bidirectional encoders because causal attention is order-sensitive (reversal-curse argument), so HardCons gains are not automatic; with joint pair decoding SoftCons becomes ~1.0 on non-NEG pairs and HardCons tracks pair accuracy, making the LLM's accuracy gains translate fully into HardCons.
integration: HF transformers AutoModelForSequenceClassification (Qwen3ForSequenceClassification, LlamaForSequenceClassification exist; Gemma 3 text classification class availability depends on transformers version - Gemma3TextForSequenceClassification or use gemma-3-1b / load text backbone [uncertain]) + peft.LoraConfig(task_type='SEQ_CLS', target_modules='all-linear', modules_to_save=['score']). Set model.config.pad_token_id (Llama has no pad token). Replace the template MLP in src/modules/model.py with a wrapper exposing forward(batch)->(logits, feature); tokenise (text1, text2) with a fixed template; produce per-row 4-way log-probs in LABELS order from src/labels.py so REVERSE_PERM applies directly for joint decoding / view pooling. Use bf16, gradient checkpointing, grouped K-fold by pair_id.
ensemble_compatibility: Yes: softmax over the 4-way head gives per-class probabilities; LLM heads are often overconfident after fine-tuning, so apply temperature scaling on grouped-CV out-of-fold predictions before pooling with encoder models or joint decoding.
inference_cost: Negligible: ~4k test rows (T1-T3 ~660 each, T4 ~4k assuming dev-like size) x 2 orders is a single forward pass each; an 8B model in bf16 labels all tracks in ~1-3 minutes on one A100; a 5-fold x 3-seed ensemble in well under an hour.
rules_disclosure: Disclose: access regime = open-weight; architecture family = decoder-only (LoRA fine-tuned); external data = public (any intermediate NLI data such as MNLI/XNLI/XNLIeu, and PhrasIS if used, must be reported). Licenses: Llama 3.x and Gemma 3 carry use policies but allow research/shared-task use; the Llama license requires 'Built with Llama' attribution and naming derivatives with a Llama prefix if redistributed. Task README allows open-weight, fine-tuned and hybrid systems; all models, data and prompts must be documented in the system paper.
contamination: Pretraining corpora of 2024-2025 LLMs likely include public iSTS 2015/2016 data and possibly PhrasIS (published 2024 with public repository), so the English phrase pairs and their source sentences may have been seen as raw text, but not DiCo labels or the new ES/EU translations (produced by the organisers via MT/LLMs plus expert verification). Label leakage risk mostly arises if a team trains on PhrasIS test-split labels that overlap DiCo test pairs; the organisers state the official evaluation split is grouped by source pair and the PhrasIS usage policy is pending. Risk for fine-tuned open LLMs: low-to-moderate [uncertain].
structural_cue_dependence: None intrinsically (row-level classifier). Only depends on pair structure if combined with joint decoding (needs twin ids, derivable from instance_id) or the singleton => NEGATIVE_OTHER cue; behaves identically if test metadata changes.
expected_gain: Main expected benefit is Weighted F1 on T2/T3/T4 (+2-6 points over mDeBERTa/XLM-R baselines [uncertain]) and a strong, diverse ensemble member with different inductive bias from encoders. Rationale: modern 7-12B LLMs carry much more lexical, taxonomic and multilingual knowledge (the pilot's dominant errors are lexico-semantic and world-knowledge failures), and LoRA makes 8B fine-tuning cheap on one GPU. Recommended order: Qwen3-8B (Apache, easy class support) and Gemma-3-12B for T1/T2/T4; Salamandra-7B (plus Latxa item) for T3/T4 Basque; Llama-3.1-8B only as a baseline. P1 not P0 because encoders plus joint decoding are cheaper first steps and LLM gains on T1 are uncertain; the decoder's order asymmetry must be neutralised with joint decoding or a bidirectional-attention variant.
